deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivation, and it is not in Riemann's hand. It is the first page of a letter ('Lieber Freund!') written after Riemann's death. From the content and the following page, it is almost certainly from Richard Dedekind to Heinrich Weber, who was editing Riemann's Werke (published 1876). The letter concerns Riemann's papers on the limiting cases of elliptic modular functions, which became Fragment XXVIII ('Fragmente über die Grenzfälle der elliptischen Modulfunctionen') with Dedekind's 'Erläuterungen'.

The writer apologises for the delay and returns two items:
(1) Riemann's manuscript 'Additamentum ad §40', with a copy. §40 most plausibly refers to Jacobi's Fundamenta Nova, where the theta and q-series expansions are treated.
(2) Folio sheets Weber had sent later, with a four-page transcription of one very faint page, read only with a magnifying glass. The other sheets are described as containing standard elliptic-function formulas and material the writer does not understand. He guesses these may be attempts at a theory of series whose general term has a logarithm cubic in the summation index, i.e. terms like exp(a n^3 + b n^2 + c n + d).

The faint page interested him because its method can be applied to the transformation of first order of the theta functions (the modular transformation tau -> -1/tau, or more generally a unimodular substitution). He had reported this a week earlier by postcard.

The next page continues:
- He found the missing correctness proof concerning sum a_nu/nu = sum a^0_nu/nu.
- He wrote everything up in 8-9 folio pages.
- He added a sketch of foundations for a new theory of modular equations, devised for complex multiplication.

Historically, these are the seeds of Dedekind's 1877 commentary on Riemann's Fragment XXVIII. That commentary treats the transformation of log eta, introduces the Dedekind sums, and gives the valence (Dedekind's modular function). The modular-equation sketch corresponds to Dedekind's 1877 'Schreiben an Herrn Borchardt über die Theorie der elliptischen Modulfunctionen'. Nothing on this page is a derivation to reconstruct.

Attribution caveat: the bundle label suggests a Riemann manuscript, but this is a later editorial letter (very likely Dedekind to Weber, c. 1874-75) about Riemann's Nachlass, not Riemann's own work.

results.what: Report that a method on a faint Riemann sheet (limiting values of modular functions / series manipulations) can be applied to the first-order transformation of theta functions
results.modern_name: Modular transformation of theta / Dedekind eta function via limiting-case (Grenzfall) analysis; precursor of the Dedekind-sum transformation law of log eta

results.what: Mention of a sketch of a new theory of modular equations aimed at complex multiplication
results.modern_name: Dedekind's theory of the modular group, fundamental domain and valence (j-invariant precursor)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an editorial cover letter (Dedekind to Weber) describing material already published in Riemann's Werke (Fragment XXVIII) and Dedekind's well-known 1876-77 commentary. It contains no new mathematics by Riemann.

checkable.sympy: tau = sympy.I*sympy.Rational(13,10); q=lambda t: sympy.exp(2*sympy.pi*sympy.I*t); eta=lambda t: q(t)**sympy.Rational(1,24)*sympy.Product(1-q(t)**n,(n,1,200)).doit(); sympy.N(eta(-1/tau) - sympy.sqrt(-sympy.I*tau)*eta(tau), 30)
checkable.asserts: First-order (tau -> -1/tau) transformation of the Dedekind eta function, the result whose general form Dedekind derived from Riemann's fragment. The value should be approximately 0.

checkable.asserts: Dedekind reciprocity law for Dedekind sums, which arose from the theta/eta transformation work referred to on this page. The value should be 0.

transcription_corrections: The transcription appears essentially accurate. Note that the hand is the letter-writer's (likely Dedekind), not Riemann's; the pencil note 'Riemann 14' and folio number '40' are archival annotations.
'Manuscript' and 'Additamentum ad §40' confirmed; 'Foliobogen', 'Vergrößerungsglas', '$\vartheta$-Functionen' and 'mittelst Karte' are correctly read.
